summary.business: Hindustan Zinc Limited is an integrated mining, smelting and captive-power company producing refined zinc, lead and silver, along with by-products such as sulphuric acid and wind power. Its metals serve automotive and stationary batteries, galvanising and construction, cable sheathing, electronics, solar photovoltaics, defence, telecommunications, railways and jewellery/investment demand in India and export markets. The company is expanding beyond its zinc-silver base into new critical minerals (rare earth elements, tungsten, potash) to become a future-facing multi-metal enterprise ("HZL 2.0").

currentContext.expansion: Hindustan Zinc's 'HZL 2.0' programme is designed to nearly double refined metal capacity from 1.144 Mtpa to 2.0 Mtpa — described as the largest expansion in company history and predominantly brownfield, leveraging the existing asset base. The Board has approved Phase 1 projects totalling around ₹17,000 crore: a 250 ktpa integrated zinc smelter at Debari, Rajasthan (with matching mines and mills capacity, investment c.₹12,000 crore, EPC partners locked in, site mobilisation started, targeted completion Q2 FY2029); India's first tailings reprocessing plant at Rampura Agucha with 10 Mtpa feed capacity (investment ₹3,823 crore, detailed engineering completed, major orders placed, targeted completion Q4 FY2028); and an exploration programme (investment c.₹1,100 crore) primarily at the Zawar and Rajpura Dariba clusters to sustain 25+ years of mine life post-expansion, with technical and drilling partners locked in. Smelting expansion beyond Phase 1 also envisages a 400 ktpa integrated zinc smelter and a 200 ktpa integrated lead smelter at existing locations. Mining and concentrator capacity is being expanded across the Rampura Agucha, Kayad, Sindesar Khurd, Rajpura Dariba and Zawar clusters through brownfield redesign and debottlenecking. At the mine level: Rampura Agucha is raising hoisting capacity from 3.75 Mtpa to 4.0 Mtpa and beneficiation capacity from 6.75 Mtpa to 7.5 Mtpa, targeting 7.5 Mtpa ore production capacity by FY2029 (up from 6.0 Mtpa); Rajpura Dariba Mine is targeting 6.0 Mtpa ore production capacity by FY2029 (up from 2.0 Mtpa) via a next-generation material-handling mechanism and new decline development; and the Zawar Group of Mines is targeting 8.0 Mtpa ore production capacity by FY2029 (up from 4.8 Mtpa), including ramping Balaria and Baroi mine production to 2.0 Mtpa. Exploration is targeting a resource base of over 500 Mnt with 250 Mnt of reserves over the long term, supported by AI/ML-based targeting, drone surveys and 3D deposit modelling. Renewable power capacity is being scaled via a 530 MW RE power-delivery agreement (with Serentica) intended to lift the renewable share of the power mix to 70%, from c.18% in FY2026. Overall growth capex for HZL 2.0 is expected at ₹40,000-50,000 crore over the next 5 years.

risks.risk: Commodity price volatility and geopolitical price shocks
risks.note: Zinc, lead and silver prices are exposed to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, Ukraine and Venezuela disrupting energy supplies and driving commodity-price volatility; management has responded by strategically hedging some expected FY2027 volumes to protect the balance sheet from pricing shocks, implying meaningful earnings sensitivity to unhedged price moves.

Aggressive US tariff hikes (with some metals facing duties up to 50%) and a broader global shift from efficiency-driven 'Just-in-Time' to resilience-led 'Just-in-Case' supply chains are disrupting traditional trade routes and raising costs for global manufacturing hubs, creating policy uncertainty that is weighing on global capital expenditure and trade volumes relevant to metal demand.

risks.risk: Rising cost of capital in a structurally higher rate environment
risks.note: Massive sovereign debt (driven by defence and tech subsidies) combined with persistent geopolitical tensions means interest rates are unlikely to return to the ultra-low levels of the past decade, necessitating agile financial strategies and selective capital allocation — a direct consideration for the Company's own long-gestation HZL 2.0 capacity expansion.

risks.risk: China and Europe structural demand slowdown
risks.note: Europe and China face structural stagnation with slower industrial recovery and subdued manufacturing activity; China's shift away from infrastructure-heavy stimulus towards a consumption-based economy is reshaping metals demand into a 'split' market, creating downside risk for demand in segments not aligned with high-tech/energy-transition end-uses.

The Company maintains dedicated Board-level oversight (Audit & Risk Management Committee, CISO, IT & Cyber Security Steering Committee) and holds cyber insurance and an incident-response retainer explicitly to protect against 'low-probability, high-impact cyberattacks', reflecting material exposure of its IT and operational-technology (OT)/plant systems to cyber threats.

risks.risk: Exposure to global trade-war dynamics and currency/import-cost pressure
risks.note: While the Company frames India as 'partially insulated' from US tariffs and the global trade slowdown due to low external leverage and new trade frameworks, it explicitly notes geopolitical tensions pose a risk to oil import costs and that global dollar strength could pressure the rupee, both of which are structural macro exposures for a metals exporter/importer of inputs.

guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Volume:** **1.1 million tonnes refined metal for FY27** — reaffirmed twice and explicitly called "our commitment." Q1 at 260kt; Q2 must "cross around 280 KT"; Q4 historically touches 280–290kt. **Silver 680 t for FY27** — implies ~175t/quarter for the remaining three; management said achieving it "will not be difficult" on better mine grades.
- **Cost:** zinc COP ex-royalty guidance held at **USD975–1,000/t** for FY27; Q1's USD851 beat it on superior by-product realisation. Management expects Q2 cost to improve further if volumes rise and sulphuric acid prices (up ~200% YoY) hold.
- **Margin:** no explicit margin target; the guided mechanism is volume-driven cost dilution.
- **Capex / commissioning dates:**
  - FY27 growth capex **USD500–600 million**.
  - **Phosphoric acid plant (Chanderiya) — commissioning in Q2 FY27.** Note: prepared remarks said the "fertilizer plant at Chanderiya" was on track for Q2; under questioning the CEO clarified only the *phosphoric acid* portion completes in Q2.
  - **Fertilizer (DAP) plant — Q1 FY28**, gated on pending environmental clearance and regulatory approvals. ~INR500cr already spent.
  - **Hot acid leaching plant, Dariba — Q2 FY27.**
  - **Tailings reprocessing plant — construction just started, ~24 months to build**, then a **6–8 month ramp**; expected output **30–35 kt of zinc**.
  - **250 KTPA integrated zinc smelter, Debari** — mine development started to match mining capacity.
  - **~650 KT new smelter + mine complex — board approval targeted in Q3 FY27, then 36 months construction; indicative capex INR24,000–25,000 cr** (extrapolated from ~INR12,000cr for 250kt; tendering underway, firm number expected in ~1 month).
  - **REE/Yttrium (Gundlupet)** — 2–3 years exploration, first production only around **2031–32**.
- **Balance sheet:** to remain a **net cash company at FY27 exit**.
- **Dividend:** policy unchanged — **minimum 30% of profit plus 5% of reserves**.
- **Operations:** **no further smelter shutdowns or planned maintenance for the remainder of FY27.**
order book & pipeline: Not applicable (commodity producer). The project pipeline is the forward book — see §8. The mineral-resource pipeline gained a rare-earth-elements and Yttrium block at Gundlupet, Karnataka, secured this quarter at G2 exploration level.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Zinc** — the volume engine; the 160,000 tpa roaster now absorbs incremental calcine demand during maintenance, plus debottlenecking at Chanderiya and Dariba. Fundamentals described as supported by constrained mine supply and steady infrastructure/galvanization/battery demand.
- **Silver** — 46% of overall profitability, the single most important earnings driver. Price moderated to USD73/oz but management is constructive medium-term on solar, electronics and electrification demand against constrained supply. Mine development is being sequenced to hit higher-PPM silver ore, maximising in Q4.
- **Lead** — 149t silver production tracked lead production; planned lead smelter maintenance fell in Q1. Fundamentals "stable"; lead averaged USD1,954/t.
- **By-products** — sulphuric acid prices up ~200% YoY and carry **no mineral royalty** (not a mineral product), which is why royalty as a share of revenue is at multi-quarter lows. By-product realisation is netted off COP and was the reason Q1 beat the cost guidance.
- **Critical minerals / fertilizers** — REE+Yttrium block (Yttrium used in red-LED phosphors and medical applications); phosphoric acid → DAP fertilizer chain at Chanderiya, converting sulphuric acid into a higher-realisation product.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **2X growth journey** — the ~650KT smelter+mine conceptualisation is its concrete expression; the Q3 FY27 board decision is the checkpoint.
- **Tailings reprocessing** — genuinely novel: management said only one mine in Australia has done it at this scale, which is why a 6–8 month ramp is assumed rather than a standard curve. 30–35kt of zinc recovered from waste is high-margin volume.
- **Critical minerals diversification** — REE/Yttrium is a decade-out option, not a near-term earnings item; management was explicit about that.
- **Fertilizers** — phosphoric acid first (Q2 FY27), DAP later (Q1 FY28).
- **Renewables** — RE consumption at 22% of energy and rising; a direct COP lever given the coal linkage shortfall. MoUs signed with Advantek Associates LLP and Aero Eagle Automobile Pvt Ltd on green hydrogen and clean energy. India's first 250-tonne electric crane deployed.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Cost leadership, quantified.** USD851/t zinc COP ex-royalty — the lowest since the underground transition and 16% below last year — against a guided band of USD975–1,000. The moat widened in a quarter when energy prices were rising.
- **Integration.** Mine-to-metal integration plus by-product recovery is what lets sulphuric acid at +200% prices and cadmium credits flow straight into the cost line; a non-integrated smelter cannot do this.
- **Grade and reserve base.** Rampura Agucha (world's largest zinc mine) and Sindesar Khurd underpin the fifth consecutive year of record Q1 mine metal.
- **Balance sheet as a competitive weapon.** Net cash INR5,572cr and INR5,253cr of pre-growth-capex FCF fund a INR24,000–25,000cr expansion without dilution or leverage stress.
- **Licence/ESG position.** Rampura Agucha became the first mine in India to receive Zinc Mark certification (after the Chanderiya smelter); first-time inclusion in the Dow Jones Best-in-Class Emerging Markets Index.
margins & cost dynamics: The 59% EBITDA margin is the output of three stacked effects: record volume, record-low COP, and a price/currency tailwind. Management's COP bridge: better grades, higher metal production, higher renewable power share and better by-product realisation, **partly offset by higher input commodity prices, especially energy**. The one deteriorating input is coal — domestic linkage materialisation collapsed to 36% from 64% in Q4, pushing the mix to costlier imported coal, which is why power & fuel rose sequentially *despite* lower production and a higher RE share. Management expects Q2 COP to improve as volumes rise above 280kt (fixed-cost dilution) and acid credits persist, but explicitly caveated "unless we are struck by higher input commodity prices, which is also a likelihood."

FY27 growth capex guided at USD500–600mn; INR800cr spent in Q1.
capital allocation: Priorities stated as unchanged and in this order: invest in high-return growth, maintain balance sheet strength, return surplus cash to shareholders. Evidence this quarter: INR11/share first interim dividend paid; net cash of INR5,572cr maintained; INR6,450cr contributed to the national exchequer in taxes, royalties and duties. The dividend policy is unchanged at a minimum 30% of profit + 5% of reserves despite the Vedanta demerger — management was asked directly and confirmed no change. The pending INR24,000–25,000cr expansion decision in Q3 is the item that will test the "return surplus cash" leg.
risks & watch-items:
- **Leadership transition.** Arun Misra hands over to Amarendu Prakash (ex-SAIL CMD, 30+ years in steel) on 1 August 2026; the CFO, Amit Gupta, is also newly appointed. A new CEO arrives precisely as a ~INR24,000cr capex decision reaches the board — strategy continuity is unproven.
- **Coal linkage failure.** 36% domestic linkage vs 64% a quarter ago is a real, unhedged cost exposure.
- **No hedging in FY27.** Management is deliberately unhedged given volatility; carried-forward positions (48kt zinc @ USD3,162, 34t silver @ USD63) sit well below spot, so they cost INR200cr in Q1 and will keep bleeding while prices stay high — but the unhedged book leaves earnings fully exposed to a price reversal.
- **Silver price moderation.** Silver fell to USD73/oz from the prior quarter's strong levels while contributing 46% of profit — the single largest earnings sensitivity.
- **SEBI observations on related-party transactions.** No penalty or restriction, but corrective measures were required. Root cause disclosed candidly: omnibus RPT approvals are set on *value*, and operating teams track *volume*, so a rising LME can breach the approved value. New SOP triggers an alarm at 80% of approved value with escalation to the Audit Committee.
- **GoI stake sale speculation.** Media reports of the government selling its ~27.92%; management deflected — "it is for the government to give the update."
- **Fertilizer plant regulatory risk.** Environmental clearance still pending; the Q1 FY28 date is contingent on it.
- **Silver WIP.** 10–15t of silver sitting in work-in-progress inflates the apparent Q1 shortfall against the 680t guide; if it does not unlock, the annual target is at risk.
management quality / tone: Precise and willing to be pinned to numbers — 1.1mn tonnes was described as "our commitment," the 650KT capex was given as an honest straight-line extrapolation with the caveat that tendering would refine it, and the REE timeline was set at 2031–32 rather than sold as a near-term story. Arun Misra corrected two analyst framings cleanly: that the company had changed its no-concentrate-sale policy (it had not — this was legacy off-grade stock), and that the whole fertilizer plant commissions in Q2 (only phosphoric acid does). The RPT explanation was unusually transparent. Outgoing-CEO tone was valedictory; the CEO-designate did not speak on the call, which leaves the strategy-continuity question open.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The prepared remarks and the Q&A disagree on the fertilizer plant: the opening script said the Chanderiya fertilizer plant was "on track to be completed by the second quarter," while the CEO later said only phosphoric acid completes in Q2 and fertilizer slips to Q1 FY28. Take the Q&A version — and treat the script as evidence that timeline discipline needs watching under the new CEO.
- Sulphuric acid is doing quiet, structural work: prices up ~200% YoY, netted off COP, and royalty-free — it is simultaneously depressing reported COP *and* depressing royalty as a percentage of revenue. A normalisation in acid prices would hit the P&L twice over.
- The concentrate sale is the cleanest read on management's opportunism: rather than derate smelters with off-grade material, they sold legacy stock into a high-LME market for INR315cr. But they flagged they will *not* repeat it if it risks starving the smelters — so this revenue line should disappear.
- Q1 at 260kt against a 1.1mn tonne guide is already 1,040kt annualised, i.e. the guidance carries a built-in buffer that Q2–Q4 seasonality (Q4 typically 280–290kt) should comfortably clear. The guide looks conservative rather than stretched.

order book & pipeline: Not applicable (commodity producer). The project pipeline is the forward book — see §8. The mineral-resource pipeline gained a rare-earth-elements and Yttrium block at Gundlupet, Karnataka, secured this quarter at G2 exploration level.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Zinc** — the volume engine; the 160,000 tpa roaster now absorbs incremental calcine demand during maintenance, plus debottlenecking at Chanderiya and Dariba. Fundamentals described as supported by constrained mine supply and steady infrastructure/galvanization/battery demand.

Price moderated to USD73/oz but management is constructive medium-term on solar, electronics and electrification demand against constrained supply. Mine development is being sequenced to hit higher-PPM silver ore, maximising in Q4.
- **Lead** — 149t silver production tracked lead production; planned lead smelter maintenance fell in Q1. Fundamentals "stable"; lead averaged USD1,954/t.
- **By-products** — sulphuric acid prices up ~200% YoY and carry **no mineral royalty** (not a mineral product), which is why royalty as a share of revenue is at multi-quarter lows. By-product realisation is netted off COP and was the reason Q1 beat the cost guidance.
- **Critical minerals / fertilizers** — REE+Yttrium block (Yttrium used in red-LED phosphors and medical applications); phosphoric acid → DAP fertilizer chain at Chanderiya, converting sulphuric acid into a higher-realisation product.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **2X growth journey** — the ~650KT smelter+mine conceptualisation is its concrete expression; the Q3 FY27 board decision is the checkpoint.
- **Tailings reprocessing** — genuinely novel: management said only one mine in Australia has done it at this scale, which is why a 6–8 month ramp is assumed rather than a standard curve. 30–35kt of zinc recovered from waste is high-margin volume.
- **Critical minerals diversification** — REE/Yttrium is a decade-out option, not a near-term earnings item; management was explicit about that.
- **Fertilizers** — phosphoric acid first (Q2 FY27), DAP later (Q1 FY28).
- **Renewables** — RE consumption at 22% of energy and rising; a direct COP lever given the coal linkage shortfall. MoUs signed with Advantek Associates LLP and Aero Eagle Automobile Pvt Ltd on green hydrogen and clean energy. India's first 250-tonne electric crane deployed.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Cost leadership, quantified.** USD851/t zinc COP ex-royalty — the lowest since the underground transition and 16% below last year — against a guided band of USD975–1,000. The moat widened in a quarter when energy prices were rising.
- **Integration.** Mine-to-metal integration plus by-product recovery is what lets sulphuric acid at +200% prices and cadmium credits flow straight into the cost line; a non-integrated smelter cannot do this.
- **Grade and reserve base.** Rampura Agucha (world's largest zinc mine) and Sindesar Khurd underpin the fifth consecutive year of record Q1 mine metal.
- **Balance sheet as a competitive weapon.** Net cash INR5,572cr and INR5,253cr of pre-growth-capex FCF fund a INR24,000–25,000cr expansion without dilution or leverage stress.
- **Licence/ESG position.** Rampura Agucha became the first mine in India to receive Zinc Mark certification (after the Chanderiya smelter); first-time inclusion in the Dow Jones Best-in-Class Emerging Markets Index.
margins & cost dynamics: The 59% EBITDA margin is the output of three stacked effects: record volume, record-low COP, and a price/currency tailwind. Management's COP bridge: better grades, higher metal production, higher renewable power share and better by-product realisation, **partly offset by higher input commodity prices, especially energy**. The one deteriorating input is coal — domestic linkage materialisation collapsed to 36% from 64% in Q4, pushing the mix to costlier imported coal, which is why power & fuel rose sequentially *despite* lower production and a higher RE share. Management expects Q2 COP to improve as volumes rise above 280kt (fixed-cost dilution) and acid credits persist, but explicitly caveated "unless we are struck by higher input commodity prices, which is also a likelihood."

capital allocation: Priorities stated as unchanged and in this order: invest in high-return growth, maintain balance sheet strength, return surplus cash to shareholders. Evidence this quarter: INR11/share first interim dividend paid; net cash of INR5,572cr maintained; INR6,450cr contributed to the national exchequer in taxes, royalties and duties. The dividend policy is unchanged at a minimum 30% of profit + 5% of reserves despite the Vedanta demerger — management was asked directly and confirmed no change. The pending INR24,000–25,000cr expansion decision in Q3 is the item that will test the "return surplus cash" leg.
risks & watch-items:
- **Leadership transition.** Arun Misra hands over to Amarendu Prakash (ex-SAIL CMD, 30+ years in steel) on 1 August 2026; the CFO, Amit Gupta, is also newly appointed. A new CEO arrives precisely as a ~INR24,000cr capex decision reaches the board — strategy continuity is unproven.
- **Coal linkage failure.** 36% domestic linkage vs 64% a quarter ago is a real, unhedged cost exposure.
- **No hedging in FY27.** Management is deliberately unhedged given volatility; carried-forward positions (48kt zinc @ USD3,162, 34t silver @ USD63) sit well below spot, so they cost INR200cr in Q1 and will keep bleeding while prices stay high — but the unhedged book leaves earnings fully exposed to a price reversal.
- **Silver price moderation.** Silver fell to USD73/oz from the prior quarter's strong levels while contributing 46% of profit — the single largest earnings sensitivity.
- **SEBI observations on related-party transactions.** No penalty or restriction, but corrective measures were required. Root cause disclosed candidly: omnibus RPT approvals are set on *value*, and operating teams track *volume*, so a rising LME can breach the approved value. New SOP triggers an alarm at 80% of approved value with escalation to the Audit Committee.
- **GoI stake sale speculation.** Media reports of the government selling its ~27.92%; management deflected — "it is for the government to give the update."
- **Fertilizer plant regulatory risk.** Environmental clearance still pending; the Q1 FY28 date is contingent on it.
- **Silver WIP.** 10–15t of silver sitting in work-in-progress inflates the apparent Q1 shortfall against the 680t guide; if it does not unlock, the annual target is at risk.
management quality / tone: Precise and willing to be pinned to numbers — 1.1mn tonnes was described as "our commitment," the 650KT capex was given as an honest straight-line extrapolation with the caveat that tendering would refine it, and the REE timeline was set at 2031–32 rather than sold as a near-term story. Arun Misra corrected two analyst framings cleanly: that the company had changed its no-concentrate-sale policy (it had not — this was legacy off-grade stock), and that the whole fertilizer plant commissions in Q2 (only phosphoric acid does). The RPT explanation was unusually transparent. Outgoing-CEO tone was valedictory; the CEO-designate did not speak on the call, which leaves the strategy-continuity question open.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The prepared remarks and the Q&A disagree on the fertilizer plant: the opening script said the Chanderiya fertilizer plant was "on track to be completed by the second quarter," while the CEO later said only phosphoric acid completes in Q2 and fertilizer slips to Q1 FY28. Take the Q&A version — and treat the script as evidence that timeline discipline needs watching under the new CEO.
- Sulphuric acid is doing quiet, structural work: prices up ~200% YoY, netted off COP, and royalty-free — it is simultaneously depressing reported COP *and* depressing royalty as a percentage of revenue. A normalisation in acid prices would hit the P&L twice over.
- The concentrate sale is the cleanest read on management's opportunism: rather than derate smelters with off-grade material, they sold legacy stock into a high-LME market for INR315cr. But they flagged they will *not* repeat it if it risks starving the smelters — so this revenue line should disappear.
- Q1 at 260kt against a 1.1mn tonne guide is already 1,040kt annualised, i.e. the guidance carries a built-in buffer that Q2–Q4 seasonality (Q4 typically 280–290kt) should comfortably clear. The guide looks conservative rather than stretched.
- Silver at 46% of profitability means this is no longer usefully modelled as a zinc company.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Hindustan Zinc Limited is an integrated mining, smelting and captive-power company producing refined zinc, lead and silver, along with by-products such as sulphuric acid and wind power. Its metals serve automotive and stationary batteries, galvanising and construction, cable sheathing, electronics, solar photovoltaics, defence, telecommunications, railways and jewellery/investment demand in India and export markets. The company is expanding beyond its zinc-silver base into new critical minerals (rare earth elements, tungsten, potash) to become a future-facing multi-metal enterprise ("HZL 2.0").

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Not applicable (commodity producer). The project pipeline is the forward book — see §8. The mineral-resource pipeline gained a rare-earth-elements and Yttrium block at Gundlupet, Karnataka, secured this quarter at G2 exploration level.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Volume:** **1.1 million tonnes refined metal for FY27** — reaffirmed twice and explicitly called "our commitment." Q1 at 260kt; Q2 must "cross around 280 KT"; Q4 historically touches 280–290kt. **Silver 680 t for FY27** — implies ~175t/quarter for the remaining three; management said achieving it "will not be difficult" on better mine grades.
- **Cost:** zinc COP ex-royalty guidance held at **USD975–1,000/t** for FY27; Q1's USD851 beat it on superior by-product realisation. Management expects Q2 cost to improve further if volumes rise and sulphuric acid prices (up ~200% YoY) hold.
- **Margin:** no explicit margin target; the guided mechanism is volume-driven cost dilution.
- **Capex / commissioning dates:**
  - FY27 growth capex **USD500–600 million**.
  - **Phosphoric acid plant (Chanderiya) — commissioning in Q2 FY27.** Note: prepared remarks said the "fertilizer plant at Chanderiya" was on track for Q2; under questioning the CEO clarified only the *phosphoric acid* portion completes in Q2.
  - **Fertilizer (DAP) plant — Q1 FY28**, gated on pending environmental clearance and regulatory approvals. ~INR500cr already spent.
  - **Hot acid leaching plant, Dariba — Q2 FY27.**
  - **Tailings reprocessing plant — construction just started, ~24 months to build**, then a **6–8 month ramp**; expected output **30–35 kt of zinc**.
  - **250 KTPA integrated zinc smelter, Debari** — mine development started to match mining capacity.
  - **~650 KT new smelter + mine complex — board approval targeted in Q3 FY27, then 36 months construction; indicative capex INR24,000–25,000 cr** (extrapolated from ~INR12,000cr for 250kt; tendering underway, firm number expected in ~1 month).
  - **REE/Yttrium (Gundlupet)** — 2–3 years exploration, first production only around **2031–32**.
- **Balance sheet:** to remain a **net cash company at FY27 exit**.
- **Dividend:** policy unchanged — **minimum 30% of profit plus 5% of reserves**.
- **Operations:** **no further smelter shutdowns or planned maintenance for the remainder of FY27.**

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **2X growth journey** — the ~650KT smelter+mine conceptualisation is its concrete expression; the Q3 FY27 board decision is the checkpoint.
- **Tailings reprocessing** — genuinely novel: management said only one mine in Australia has done it at this scale, which is why a 6–8 month ramp is assumed rather than a standard curve. 30–35kt of zinc recovered from waste is high-margin volume.
- **Critical minerals diversification** — REE/Yttrium is a decade-out option, not a near-term earnings item; management was explicit about that.
- **Fertilizers** — phosphoric acid first (Q2 FY27), DAP later (Q1 FY28).
- **Renewables** — RE consumption at 22% of energy and rising; a direct COP lever given the coal linkage shortfall. MoUs signed with Advantek Associates LLP and Aero Eagle Automobile Pvt Ltd on green hydrogen and clean energy. India's first 250-tonne electric crane deployed.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Zinc demand driven by galvanising (c.60% of use), infrastructure and construction, national programmes (Gati Shakti, National Infrastructure Pipeline), road/rail modernisation, and rising auto/appliance production
- India targeting 300 Mnt crude steel capacity by 2030 under the National Steel Policy is expected to proportionately grow domestic zinc demand, underpinning the company's capacity-doubling plan
- Global zinc mine output expected to remain tight, plateauing by CY2028 and declining from CY2029, supporting prices even as refined supply/China smelting capacity growth eases prices from CY2027
- Silver demand structurally shifting towards technology-led applications (AI infrastructure, solar, electronics, 5G), with a persistent multi-year global supply deficit supporting prices; India is the largest global silver consumer
- Lead demand anchored in automotive SLI/replacement batteries, stationary battery applications (data centres, telecom, grid storage), and India's own consumption led by batteries, cables and galvanisers
- Critical minerals (REE, tungsten, potash) demand accelerating with the energy transition and technology growth, against India's significant import dependence
- India remains the key macro growth engine: FY2026 GDP growth of c.7.5%, FY2027 projected at 6.4-6.9%, supported by strong domestic demand, government infrastructure spending and the 'China+1' manufacturing shift, with benign inflation supporting a neutral-to-easing RBI stance
- Around 70% of refined zinc and almost 100% of silver production is sold domestically, insulating the company from global price/demand volatility
- Management expects a phase of 'cautious optimism' heading into FY2027: a tepid global economic environment but commodity markets offering upside from steady downstream demand, with India's infrastructure investment, rising steel demand and energy-transition/technology-led industrial activity sustaining commodity demand
- Board-approved Phase 1 HZL 2.0 expansion projects totalling around ₹17,000 crore are in execution, with EPC partners finalised and site mobilisation underway for the Debari smelter expansion and the Rampura Agucha tailings reprocessing plant
- Overall growth capex pipeline of ₹40,000-50,000 crore planned over the next 5 years under HZL 2.0

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: The 59% EBITDA margin is the output of three stacked effects: record volume, record-low COP, and a price/currency tailwind. Management's COP bridge: better grades, higher metal production, higher renewable power share and better by-product realisation, **partly offset by higher input commodity prices, especially energy**. The one deteriorating input is coal — domestic linkage materialisation collapsed to 36% from 64% in Q4, pushing the mix to costlier imported coal, which is why power & fuel rose sequentially *despite* lower production and a higher RE share. Management expects Q2 COP to improve as volumes rise above 280kt (fixed-cost dilution) and acid credits persist, but explicitly caveated "unless we are struck by higher input commodity prices, which is also a likelihood."

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Priorities stated as unchanged and in this order: invest in high-return growth, maintain balance sheet strength, return surplus cash to shareholders. Evidence this quarter: INR11/share first interim dividend paid; net cash of INR5,572cr maintained; INR6,450cr contributed to the national exchequer in taxes, royalties and duties. The dividend policy is unchanged at a minimum 30% of profit + 5% of reserves despite the Vedanta demerger — management was asked directly and confirmed no change. The pending INR24,000–25,000cr expansion decision in Q3 is the item that will test the "return surplus cash" leg.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Hindustan Zinc's 'HZL 2.0' programme is designed to nearly double refined metal capacity from 1.144 Mtpa to 2.0 Mtpa — described as the largest expansion in company history and predominantly brownfield, leveraging the existing asset base. The Board has approved Phase 1 projects totalling around ₹17,000 crore: a 250 ktpa integrated zinc smelter at Debari, Rajasthan (with matching mines and mills capacity, investment c.₹12,000 crore, EPC partners locked in, site mobilisation started, targeted completion Q2 FY2029); India's first tailings reprocessing plant at Rampura Agucha with 10 Mtpa feed capacity (investment ₹3,823 crore, detailed engineering completed, major orders placed, targeted completion Q4 FY2028); and an exploration programme (investment c.₹1,100 crore) primarily at the Zawar and Rajpura Dariba clusters to sustain 25+ years of mine life post-expansion, with technical and drilling partners locked in. Smelting expansion beyond Phase 1 also envisages a 400 ktpa integrated zinc smelter and a 200 ktpa integrated lead smelter at existing locations. Mining and concentrator capacity is being expanded across the Rampura Agucha, Kayad, Sindesar Khurd, Rajpura Dariba and Zawar clusters through brownfield redesign and debottlenecking. At the mine level: Rampura Agucha is raising hoisting capacity from 3.75 Mtpa to 4.0 Mtpa and beneficiation capacity from 6.75 Mtpa to 7.5 Mtpa, targeting 7.5 Mtpa ore production capacity by FY2029 (up from 6.0 Mtpa); Rajpura Dariba Mine is targeting 6.0 Mtpa ore production capacity by FY2029 (up from 2.0 Mtpa) via a next-generation material-handling mechanism and new decline development; and the Zawar Group of Mines is targeting 8.0 Mtpa ore production capacity by FY2029 (up from 4.8 Mtpa), including ramping Balaria and Baroi mine production to 2.0 Mtpa. Exploration is targeting a resource base of over 500 Mnt with 250 Mnt of reserves over the long term, supported by AI/ML-based targeting, drone surveys and 3D deposit modelling. Renewable power capacity is being scaled via a 530 MW RE power-delivery agreement (with Serentica) intended to lift the renewable share of the power mix to 70%, from c.18% in FY2026. Overall growth capex for HZL 2.0 is expected at ₹40,000-50,000 crore over the next 5 years.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Precise and willing to be pinned to numbers — 1.1mn tonnes was described as "our commitment," the 650KT capex was given as an honest straight-line extrapolation with the caveat that tendering would refine it, and the REE timeline was set at 2031–32 rather than sold as a near-term story. Arun Misra corrected two analyst framings cleanly: that the company had changed its no-concentrate-sale policy (it had not — this was legacy off-grade stock), and that the whole fertilizer plant commissions in Q2 (only phosphoric acid does). The RPT explanation was unusually transparent. Outgoing-CEO tone was valedictory; the CEO-designate did not speak on the call, which leaves the strategy-continuity question open.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- India's leading lead producer, with expected domestic primary market share rising to 92% in FY2026 from 74% in FY2025, backed by long-term offtake contracts with large battery manufacturers
- Only primary silver producer in India and among the top 10 silver producers globally, with silver production up over 20x in two decades
- Global cost leadership: zinc cost of production reduced 9% YoY to a 5-year low of US$ 959 per tonne, described as amongst the lowest globally
- Industry-leading EBITDA margin of c.54% in FY2026, up from c.51% in FY2025
- Record resource base underpins mine life: highest-ever ore Resources & Reserves of 468.6 Mnt and highest-ever metal reserves (13.9 Mnt) since the underground transition
- Ranked 1st globally in the S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment 2025 (Metals & Mining sector) for the 3rd consecutive year, and first Indian company admitted to the International Council on Mining & Metals (ICMM)

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **Leadership transition.** Arun Misra hands over to Amarendu Prakash (ex-SAIL CMD, 30+ years in steel) on 1 August 2026; the CFO, Amit Gupta, is also newly appointed. A new CEO arrives precisely as a ~INR24,000cr capex decision reaches the board — strategy continuity is unproven.
- **Coal linkage failure.** 36% domestic linkage vs 64% a quarter ago is a real, unhedged cost exposure.
- **No hedging in FY27.** Management is deliberately unhedged given volatility; carried-forward positions (48kt zinc @ USD3,162, 34t silver @ USD63) sit well below spot, so they cost INR200cr in Q1 and will keep bleeding while prices stay high — but the unhedged book leaves earnings fully exposed to a price reversal.
- **Silver price moderation.** Silver fell to USD73/oz from the prior quarter's strong levels while contributing 46% of profit — the single largest earnings sensitivity.
- **SEBI observations on related-party transactions.** No penalty or restriction, but corrective measures were required. Root cause disclosed candidly: omnibus RPT approvals are set on *value*, and operating teams track *volume*, so a rising LME can breach the approved value. New SOP triggers an alarm at 80% of approved value with escalation to the Audit Committee.
- **GoI stake sale speculation.** Media reports of the government selling its ~27.92%; management deflected — "it is for the government to give the update."
- **Fertilizer plant regulatory risk.** Environmental clearance still pending; the Q1 FY28 date is contingent on it.
- **Silver WIP.** 10–15t of silver sitting in work-in-progress inflates the apparent Q1 shortfall against the 680t guide; if it does not unlock, the annual target is at risk.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- The prepared remarks and the Q&A disagree on the fertilizer plant: the opening script said the Chanderiya fertilizer plant was "on track to be completed by the second quarter," while the CEO later said only phosphoric acid completes in Q2 and fertilizer slips to Q1 FY28. Take the Q&A version — and treat the script as evidence that timeline discipline needs watching under the new CEO.
- Sulphuric acid is doing quiet, structural work: prices up ~200% YoY, netted off COP, and royalty-free — it is simultaneously depressing reported COP *and* depressing royalty as a percentage of revenue. A normalisation in acid prices would hit the P&L twice over.
- The concentrate sale is the cleanest read on management's opportunism: rather than derate smelters with off-grade material, they sold legacy stock into a high-LME market for INR315cr. But they flagged they will *not* repeat it if it risks starving the smelters — so this revenue line should disappear.
- Q1 at 260kt against a 1.1mn tonne guide is already 1,040kt annualised, i.e. the guidance carries a built-in buffer that Q2–Q4 seasonality (Q4 typically 280–290kt) should comfortably clear. The guide looks conservative rather than stretched.
- Silver at 46% of profitability means this is no longer usefully modelled as a zinc company.
